messages:
Maya (Finance): Heads up — AcmeCorp reported they were charged full committed GPU fees on this month's invoice even though they have an active reserved commitment credit. Invoice line shows credits = $0. Can someone look into why credits didn't apply?
Chris (Infra): I saw an anomalous billing alert this morning for the reserved pool. Quick note: some clusters were spun up in us-west2 while the commitment was purchased for us-west1. Could be region mismatch.
Jin (Cloud): Pulling invoice lines now. Matching by commitment id: `R-ACME-2023`. Invoice 2026-03-02 line items show the commitment applied to project `acme-prod-uswest2` but the billing account's commitment config is scoped to `us-west1`. Snippet:```
RESOURCE: compute.googleapis.com/commitment/R-ACME-2023
PROJECT: projects/acme-prod-uswest2
REGION: us-west2
CREDIT_APPLIED: $0.00
```
Maya (Finance): Ugh. Client is asking for an explanation and a refund/credit. Can GCP do a retroactive re-assignment of credit if it's just a tagging/region mismatch?
Jin (Cloud): Usually support will do one-off adjustments if it's provable mis-tagging. Opened a ticket with GCP Support: case 1234567890. Attached invoice PDF and commit IDs. BillingBot: Case 1234567890 created, expected initial response within 48 hours.
Elena (Acct Mgmt): I'll notify the account team and the customer. They want either a GCP-side correction or Redwood offsetting the overage while case is pending. How big is the hit?
Chris (Infra): Quick calc from cluster telemetry: extra billed GPU hours ~320 hrs (burst instances that landed in us-west2). Estimated overage ~$14,200. Could be ±10% depending on preemptible mix.
Maya (Finance): That's material but doable. Finance can issue a one-time promo credit to the customer's account to cover the amount while we wait on support. Need to log it against contract credits and mark as pending cloud reimbursement if GCP agrees.
Jin (Cloud): I'll add the following to the support case: evidence of project/region mismatch, terraform state show where `billing_region` var resolved to `us-west2`, and instance creation timestamps. If GCP requires a signed statement we can provide it.
Chris (Infra): Root cause note — our cluster bootstrap has a fallback that tries to pick the nearest region and falls back to a `dyn` choice; recently the mapping table returned `us-west2`. I'll push a fix to the bootstrap to enforce `billing_region` and emit a tagging validation error. Plan: remediation script + validation check.
Elena (Acct Mgmt): I will draft a customer-facing message: explain we're investigating, will offset the invoice temporarily, and follow up when GCP responds. Will ask for patience and provide case #.
Maya (Finance): Action items: 1) Jin attach support case # and invoice PDF to this thread; 2) Elena send the customer note within 2 hours and confirm they accept temporary offset; 3) Chris deploy the tagging validation and remediation script; 4) Finance will create a pending promo credit entry for $14,200 in the ledger labelled `pending-gcp-reconcile`.
BillingBot: Support case 1234567890 updated: customer-supplied evidence uploaded (invoice, terraform state).
Jin (Cloud): Also discovered a secondary issue: some older dedicated commitments were region-qualified at the billing account level but per-project labels were missing which prevents automated credit fallthrough. I'll run a tag audit across `acme-*` projects and post results.
Chris (Infra): I'll create a small playbook for infra to check `billing_region` and `commitment_id` at cluster creation time. Will post PR to `infra/ops` and ping here.
Maya (Finance): If GCP denies retroactive credit, we will honor the promo credit and then classify it as an extraordinary credit for Q1; finance will need jira + approval. Keep updates in this thread.
Elena (Acct Mgmt): Sent draft to customer, they acknowledged and appreciate the temporary offset. Will wait for GCP reply. :+1:
Maya (Finance): Thanks. Please post the audit output and the remediation PR links here when available so we can close the loop and update internal KB for commitments handling.
